title: Acting and Reacting in Different Situations (2)

instruction.text: Put yourself in the following situation.

atoms.text: You promised your friend Sinjun that you would ride your bike with him after school. Later that afternoon, you are invited to go with another friend for ice cream. What do you do?

instruction.text: Sort the actions from best to worst, starting with the best option on top.

feedback.end: Keeping your promises is important. When you keep your promises, people feel like they can rely on you and that you are trustworthy. These are very good traits to have. In this situation, you could have also asked your other friend whether Sinjun could come too.

atoms.text: You tell your other friend that you already have plans, but that you would like to go another time. Then you meet Sinjun to ride your bikes.
You tell Sinjun that you are sorry, but that you have to reschedule your biking plans.
You forget about your plans with Sinjun and go for ice cream.

instruction.text: Put yourself in the following situation.

atoms.text: You forgot your money to buy some chips after school. Your friend offers to pay for your chips and says that you can pay her back another time. What do you do?

instruction.text: Sort the actions from best to worst, starting with the best option on top.

feedback.end: When someone is kind and lends you money, you should try to pay them back as soon as possible. It is okay to forget for a few days, but the sooner you do it, the less likely you are to forget. This is a good habit to develop and makes you a trustworthy person.

atoms.text: I pay her back the next day.
I pay her back next week. I forgot for the first few days.
I wait for her to ask for the money back. Maybe she will forget, and then the chips are free.

instruction.text: Put yourself in the following situation.

atoms.text: Your friend wants to walk to a new park that is further away and where you’ve never been. What do you do?

instruction.text: Sort the actions from best to worst, starting with the best option on top.

feedback.end: It can be tempting to rush into things. However, exercising a bit of caution is important to prevent bad things from happening and to avoid getting into trouble.

atoms.text: Ask a parent first. They probably don’t want you going too far away without knowing where you are going.
Leave a note telling your parents where you are going, but don’t wait for permission.
Agree and decide to leave for the park right away.

instruction.text: Put yourself in the following situation.

atoms.text: Your sister went into your room for the hundredth time without asking. She knows this upsets you and you are furious. What do you do?

instruction.text: Sort the actions from best to worst, starting with the best option on top.

feedback.end: Trying to calmly solve the situation yourself would be the best option. Things can get a bit trickier when your sibling doesn’t listen to you. What would you do in this situation?

atoms.text: You take a deep breath, calm down for a moment, and then politely ask her to leave your room.
You run angrily to a parent so that they can handle the situation.
You start yelling until she cries.

instruction.text: What could you do if your sister doesn’t listen to you when you ask her to leave? Choose the three actions you could take to manage the problem.

b: ++You sit down with your sister in a calm moment and talk about how it feels when she invades your space.
++You create a plan as a family about what will happen if she enters without permission again.
You hope it goes away by itself.
